    What happened to Virginia's basketball coach?

    AI Overview
    Tony Bennett, the winningest coach in Virginia men's basketball history, announced his retirement on October 18, 2024, just before the 2024-25 season, citing that he was no longer the best person to lead the program in the current era of college sports. He left after 15 seasons, having led UVA to the 2019 NCAA Championship. 
    This video shows Tony Bennett explaining his decision to retire:
    01:09
    WDBJ7
    YouTube• Oct 21, 2024
    Key Details regarding the retirement: 
    • Reason for Leaving: Bennett expressed that the changing landscape of college sports (NIL, transfer portal) made him feel like "a square peg in a round hole".
    • Immediate Move: His retirement was effective immediately, just weeks before the season opener, shocking the college basketball world.
    • Succession: Associate head coach Ron Sanchez was named interim head coach for the 2024-25 season.
    • Legacy: During his 15-year tenure (364-136 record), Bennett won a national championship, two ACC Tournament titles, and six ACC regular-season championships. 
    Following his retirement, reports as of January 2026 indicate Bennett has no regrets about his decision and is enjoying life after coaching.
